pass_rule: all core questions substantially correct in the learner's own words; stretch questions inform the grade, not the gate

questions.prompt: You just installed the Go toolchain. How do you prove the installation actually worked, and why do we check in a new terminal rather than trusting the installer?
expected_points: run go version and read the version line
installers change startup configuration that open terminals never re-read
a version line proves the tool is both installed and reachable via PATH

questions.prompt: What is an environment variable? Walk me through creating one that is still there after you close the terminal and open a new one.
expected_points: a named text value the shell hands to every program it starts
export NAME=value sets it for the current session only
persistence means putting the export line in the shell profile (~/.zshrc or ~/.bashrc)
verify in a new terminal with echo "$NAME"

questions.prompt: A friend installs a tool, but typing its name gives 'command not found'. What is most likely going on, and how do you fix it?
expected_points: the shell searches only the directories listed in PATH, in order
the tool's directory is probably not on PATH, not missing from disk
diagnose with command -v and by printing PATH
fix by appending the directory to PATH in the shell profile, then opening a new terminal

questions.prompt: You are starting a brand-new project. Which folders and files do you create before writing any real code, and why git init on day one?
expected_points: one subdirectory per project inside a single projects home
README.md describing the project and .gitignore for build outputs
for Go, go mod init creating go.mod
git init immediately so every experiment is recorded and undoable

questions.prompt: The exercise ended with building and running a tiny program you don't fully understand yet. What did that step prove, and why is it worth doing before learning the language?
expected_points: it exercises the whole chain end to end: editor, toolchain, build, run, git
if the smallest program works, future failures are in the code, not the setup
understanding the program text was not the point — that comes next stage

questions.prompt: go version already works, so why did check.sh also demand that $(go env GOPATH)/bin be on PATH?
expected_points: the go command and go-installed tools live in different directories
tools like gopls are installed into GOPATH/bin, which is often not on PATH by default
without it the language works but editor tooling mysteriously fails

questions.prompt: You add an export line to ~/.zshrc, but echo still prints nothing. Name two different causes and how you'd tell them apart.
expected_points: still in the old terminal — the profile is only read at startup, so open a new one
wrong profile for the shell in use — check echo $SHELL
a typo in the line itself — re-read the file, or watch for errors when a new terminal opens
